Calculate confidence intervals

Source: R/stats.R
conf_int.Rd

Calculates confidence intervals for each distribution-estimation result in `df`. Normal, Lognormal, and Nonparametric distributions are dispatched to the corresponding EnvStats estimation function. Censored Normal and Lognormal data are dispatched to the corresponding censored-data method when `censored_col` identifies censored observations.

Usage

conf_int(
  df,
  method = "mvue",
  ci_type = "lower",
  ci_param = "mean",
  conf_level = 0.95,
  analysis_result = ".analysis_result",
  censored_col = NULL,
  censored_args = list(censoring.side = "left"),
  nonparametric_args = list(p = 0.5, type = 7, lcl.rank = NULL, ucl.rank = NULL, lb =
    -Inf, ub = Inf, ci.method = "interpolate", min.coverage = TRUE, tol = 0)
)

Arguments

df

A data frame returned by [est_dist()] with `keep_data_object = TRUE`.

method

Character string specifying the estimation method passed to EnvStats.

ci_type

Character string specifying the confidence-interval type. Supported values are `"two-sided"`, `"upper"`, and `"lower"`.

ci_param

Character string specifying the parameter for which the interval is calculated, such as `"mean"`, `"median"`, `"quantile"`, or `"geometric.mean"`, depending on the selected EnvStats function.

conf_level

A scalar between 0 and 1 specifying the confidence level.

analysis_result

Character scalar giving the name of the result column inside each nested data frame.

censored_col

Optional character scalar giving the name of a logical censoring-indicator column inside each nested data frame. `TRUE` identifies a censored observation.

censored_args

Named list of additional arguments passed to the censored EnvStats function. For left-censored groundwater data, use `list(censoring.side = "left")`.

nonparametric_args

Named list of additional arguments passed to [EnvStats::eqnpar()].

Value

A data frame containing the grouping columns from `df`, the estimated distribution, sample size, confidence level, and confidence limits:

  • `lcl`: lower confidence limit;

  • `ucl`: upper confidence limit;

  • `sample_size`: number of observations used;

  • `conf_level`: confidence level.

Details

The input must be generated by [est_dist()] with `keep_data_object = TRUE`.

See also

[est_dist()], [tol_int()], [EnvStats::enorm()], [EnvStats::elnorm()], [EnvStats::eqnpar()]

Examples

# \donttest{
data("gw_data")

background_data <- gw_data |>
  dplyr::filter(
    location_id %in% c("MW-1", "MW-2", "MW-3", "MW-4"),
    param_name %in% c(
      "Sulfate, total",
      "Arsenic, dissolved",
      "Boron, dissolved"
    ),
    sample_date >= lubridate::ymd("2007-12-20"),
    sample_date <= lubridate::ymd("2012-01-01")
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    location_id,
    param_name,
    default_unit
  ) |>
  percent_lt() |>
  est_dist(keep_data_object = TRUE)
#> Error in est_dist(percent_lt(dplyr::group_by(dplyr::filter(gw_data, location_id %in%     c("MW-1", "MW-2", "MW-3", "MW-4"), param_name %in% c("Sulfate, total",     "Arsenic, dissolved", "Boron, dissolved"), sample_date >=     lubridate::ymd("2007-12-20"), sample_date <= lubridate::ymd("2012-01-01")),     location_id, param_name, default_unit)), keep_data_object = TRUE): could not find function "est_dist"

conf_int(
  background_data,
  ci_type = "upper",
  ci_param = "mean",
  conf_level = 0.99
)
#> Error in conf_int(background_data, ci_type = "upper", ci_param = "mean",     conf_level = 0.99): unused argument (ci_param = "mean")
# }
